governance.attested_by: miso13 manitoba-firm-peryear 2026-06-26 (KEEPER on faithfulness grounds, supersedes miso12-seam-deliverability)
governance.note: ONE lever on top of miso12 (seam-deliverability): replace the FLAT Manitoba Hydro firm-import block (1400 MW must-flow, ~12.3 TWh/yr, the forecast-native MIDPOINT of Manitoba's 10-15 TWh/yr US export band) with a MEASURED per-year firm-hydro DELIVERY, backcast-only. THE MEASURED INPUT: data/raw/eia-930-interchange/'MISO interchange hourly.parquet' (the SAME EIA-930 directed BA-to-BA INTERCHANGE product the per-seam deliverability envelope uses), filtered to the MHEB (Manitoba Hydro) DIBA; EIA sign + = MISO exports to MHEB, so the firm IMPORT is the negative-flow hours, import_mw = -min(mw,0). The GROSS directed firm import, annualized flat at 8760 h, is constants.MISO_MANITOBA_FIRM_IMPORT_MW_BY_YEAR = {2023: 726, 2024: 531, 2025: 224} MW (= 6.36 / 4.65 / 1.96 TWh). This captures Manitoba's well-documented multi-year DROUGHT (low Nelson/Winnipeg River runoff through 2024-2025 collapsed its firm southbound exports — Manitoba Hydro reported sharply reduced US exports and even net imports). transmission.build_miso_firm_imports(iso, year, mode) sizes the block via constants.resolve_miso_manitoba_firm_import_mw: the measured per-year MW in backcast mode, the flat 1400 MW contract midpoint in forecast (byte-identical forward). The must-flow floor (inject_miso_firm_imports) scales off pmax, so it now floors at the measured per-year level. NOT A RESIDUAL FIT (rules #11/#12): the GROSS firm DELIVERY is a physical hydro-availability / firm-contract quantity computed from the directed-flow series BEFORE any LP runs; it is regenerable for a forward year from Manitoba's hydro outlook + the contract and is flow-responsive (the 2025 drought collapse is the INPUT changing, not a tune to MISO's net-MWh). It is the GROSS firm import (not the net MHEB interchange): the contract still delivers ~2 TWh in drought-2025, while MISO's occasional surplus sell-back to Manitoba is a separate, seam-excluded transaction, not a reason to net the firm block negative. This is the SAME admissibility class already accepted for the nuclear refuel derate (NUCLEAR_MONTHLY_CF_BY_YEAR) and the seam deliverability envelope (MISO_SEAM_DIBA). Reproduce / re-check end-to-end with scripts/derive_manitoba_firm_import.py --check (asserts the committed table still matches the data within 1 MW). RESULT (net interchange, EIA + = export): 2023 -47.9 (miso12) -> -43.9 (actual -37.9) = the structural over-import shrinks toward measured; 2024 -25.1 -> -19.8 (actual -23.1) with the IMPORT COMPOSITION corrected, not just the total: per-seam net import Manitoba +12.3 -> +4.65 (measured +3.0, near-exact) and the freed ~7.6 TWh raises MISO's own LMP so the PJM seam imports MORE, +8.4 -> +10.5 toward measured +32.2 (the predicted reinforcement -- removing phantom cheap injection lifts MISO's dual and pulls the under-priced eastern import up). The faithful per-year cap also EXPOSES (does not cause) the now-fully-isolated dominant miss: in dear-gas 2025 it removes the ~10 TWh phantom Manitoba import that was MASKING the COAL OVER-RUN, so 2025 flips to net export +14.4 (actual -19.0) with coal 239.7 vs 201.0 EIA-923 (+38.6 TWh) -- the model gas is already near-exact (211.4 vs 207.6 EIA-923), so the 2025 miss is unambiguously the dear-gas coal OFFER level, the separate next lever. Kept on rule-#11/#1 grounds: the accurate measured firm delivery replaces a flat estimate that was SILENTLY COMPENSATING for the coal over-run; the worse 2025 fit is the discovered bug surfacing, not a regression to revert. No outage change; the historic CAMPD unit-outage overlay is unchanged.
governance.validation_note: Reproducible end-to-end: (1) scripts/derive_manitoba_firm_import.py --years 2023 2024 2025 --check prints gross_import 6.357/4.649/1.964 TWh -> 725.7/530.7/224.2 MW and asserts the committed MISO_MANITOBA_FIRM_IMPORT_MW_BY_YEAR matches within 1 MW; (2) build_miso_firm_imports('MISO', year, 'backcast') returns pmax 726/531/224 MW, ('MISO', year, 'forecast') and any forecast year return the flat 1400 MW (forward byte-identical); MISO-only (empty for every other ISO). (3) The LP run log prints 'MISO <year>: Manitoba firm-hydro import baseload floored (must-flow)' at the reduced per-year level. Tests: tests/test_miso_firm_imports.py (forecast keeps flat contract MW; backcast uses measured per-year delivery, 2025 << 2023 << flat; resolver matches build; the firm floor still scales off pmax) all pass with the existing seam/floor tests. Per-seam model-vs-measured net import (positive=import, 2024, scratchpad verify from dispatch/2024_P1.parquet): PJM +10.5 vs +32.2 / SPP +4.7 vs -0.4 / South +0.0 vs -11.8 / Manitoba +4.65 vs +3.0; total -19.8 vs actual -23.1. Renders against the corrected EIA-930 benchmark (geo/biomass fold-in deflation live). P2 commitment off (meta.passes=[P1], MISO default). Solved 2023/2024/2025 in one --year invocation to results/calibration/MISO/manitoba_firm (per-year RSS peaked ~10 GB, released between years; no cross-year dependency).
governance.git_note: Lever is config-gated by mode + year, no new flag: scenarios stays as-is; constants.resolve_miso_manitoba_firm_import_mw returns the measured per-year MW only in mode=='backcast' with year in MISO_MANITOBA_FIRM_IMPORT_MW_BY_YEAR, else the flat MISO_MANITOBA_FIRM_IMPORT_MW. MISO-only (build_miso_firm_imports returns nothing otherwise) and forecast byte-identical for every ISO and year.

model_miss_notes: The exceptions ledger is EMPTY by design: every out-of-tolerance criterion is a genuine MODEL MISS to fix in a later lever, NOT an accepted measured-input limitation, so the determination is honestly NOT-YET (same posture as miso12). The now-ISOLATED misses and their separate next levers: (1) DOMINANT -- 2025 dear-gas COAL OVER-RUN: coal 239.7 vs 201.0 EIA-923 (+38.6 TWh) drives MISO net-LONG so it net-EXPORTS (+14.4 vs actual -19.0 import); model gas is already near-exact (211.4 vs 207.6), so the root cause is the coal OFFER level in dear gas (PRB passthrough sigmoid / coal take-or-pay), NOT the import level -- this lever correctly UNMASKS the coal length by removing the phantom Manitoba import that hid it. (2) South seam structurally under-exports all years (model ~0 vs measured -11.8 in 2024): the MISO-South / Entergy<->SOCO border is priced as a SERC bilateral estimate (HR 12.0, no organized-market LMP) and never carries MISO's real southern export -- a South-seam pricing lever. (3) SPP seam over-imports (2024 +4.7 vs measured -0.4): residual SPP neighbor-price level after the per-year HR anchor. (4) PJM seam still under-imports (+10.5 vs +32.2) though improved -- the per-year PJM HR anchor 13.49 over-prices the dear-2024 hub relative to the realized eastern transfer; a neighbor-price item, not closable by a residual adder. (5) No ORDC/scarcity tail in MISO yet (0 scarcity hours). None of these is closable by an adder/haircut/pin/rescale to a residual (rule #12).
